valuationInputs.name: Beta
valuationInputs.reason: 8 steps, 14 Nov 2026. (1) Business: a Sri Lankan commercial bank (the bank is about 93% of group profit; Siyapatha Finance and small subsidiaries the rest), so one sector beta. (2)–(3) A bank, so no relevering: the sector's levered beta is used. Damodaran's emerging-markets dataset (betaEmerg) could NOT be opened: his site is blocked by this run's network settings. A web-search extract of his January 2026 sector betas gives Bank (Money Center) levered 0.70 (604 firms); it couldn't be confirmed whether that row is the emerging-markets or the global file. (4) Local 5-year betas from web-search extracts (pages not opened): StockAnalysis 0.55, Investing.com 0.52, Simply Wall St 0.52 (dated April 2025); median 0.52. Not thinly traded. (5) Higher of 0.70 and 0.52 = 0.70. (6) Within 0.3–2. (7) Into the formula by scripts/reinvestment.py. Provisional: refresh in January 2027 with Damodaran's emerging-markets file and three verified local 5-year betas.

valuationInputs.name: Cost of equity
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py (14 Nov 2026): 8.24% + 0.70 × (4.2% + 6.08%) = 15.4%, ±1.5 points. Replaces the hand-set 20 / 18 / 16.5%.

valuationInputs.name: Growth check
valuationInputs.value: Assumed 6% / 9% / 11%; supported 11.3% (share of profit kept × ROE, FY 2025: 62.9% × 17.9%). All within 2 pts.
valuationInputs.reason: From scripts/reinvestment.py on the FY 2025 figures; growth for the next five years.

valuationInputs.name: Long-run ROE (price to book)
valuationInputs.reason: Cut a point from 15 / 17 / 19%: reported 2026 ROE (18.4%) is flattered by the tax settlement (about 16.5% at a normal rate), and capital is tightening.

valuationInputs.name: ROE path (residual income)
valuationInputs.reason: One starting ROE for every case (scripts/valuation.py takes a single roeStart): 16.5%, the 2026 bank ROE with a normal tax rate (18.4% reported). Moves in a straight line to the long-run ROE over 10 years; then the excess return grows at the long-run rate.

valuationInputs.name: Long-term growth
valuationInputs.reason: Below the 12.24% bond yield and the cost of equity; needs 33–39% of profit kept (growth ÷ ROE).

valuationInputs.name: 2027 EPS × P/E
valuationInputs.reason: 2026 pre-tax profit flat; 2027 pre-tax 0% / +10% / +18% with tax back near 38%. Bear 12% below the Rs 30.66 run-rate because the run-rate includes the prior-year tax settlement. P/Es within the 2022–2025 range and below justified P/E.

valuationInputs.name: Dividends
valuationInputs.value: Next year Rs 10.0 / 11.3 / 12.4 (37% of 2027 EPS), growing 6% / 9% / 11% for five years, then 5% / 6% / 7%; payout stays 37%
valuationInputs.reason: After the five growth years the payout becomes 1 − long-run growth ÷ ROE (Damodaran's two-stage dividend model): 64.3% / 62.5% / 61.1%, from long-run growth 5/6/7% and long-run ROE 14/16/18% (the 'Long-run ROE (price to book)' input), on EPS 27/30.5/33.5 (the '2027 EPS × P/E' input). Corrected 2026-11-21: before, the code kept the high-growth payout forever. Earlier reason: Now worked by scripts/valuation.py, whose dividend model can't raise the payout after five years, so the 1 − growth ÷ ROE step-up of 14 November is dropped. Conservative: retained profit beyond growth needs isn't counted (with the step-up the method gave about Rs 194). Dividend growth stays within the 11.3% supported.

openQuestions: Full-year 2026 (due February 2027): final dividend, and whether it stays in cash with CET1 at 12.3%.
Does the tax rate return to about 38% in 2027, or is part of the 2026 saving lasting?
Pre-tax profit growth: flat in nine months of 2026; does it return in Q4 and 2027?
Impairments as the 2026 loan growth (22%) seasons.
Beta: recheck in January 2027 with Damodaran's emerging-markets bank beta and three verified local 5-year betas.
Any new taxes on banks in the 2027 budget.
Cost-to-income: management promises below the industry average in the medium term; 44.3% in nine months of 2026 and rising.
Shareholders: any change in the four big holders (Vallibel One, Phantom Investments, Mr Y S H I Silva, EPF, about 45% together).

changeLog.summary: First analysis. Price corrected to the CSE close of Rs 152.00 (6 Nov 2026) from a stale web snapshot of Rs 137.25; the valuation is unchanged.

Q3 confirmed the first half: 9M group EPS Rs 22.63 (+15%). Questions answered: profit held up in Q3 (+15%) despite the H1 one-offs; CET1 fell further to 12.27% and Rs 10bn Tier 2 debentures were raised; Stage 3 kept falling (6.07%). NAV Rs 173.18 lifted the P/B and residual-income methods; 2026 EPS range narrowed to 29/31/32. Business tests 4 of 4; category unchanged (watch list).

Requested from Telegram (/redo samp full). Research record rebuilt from the four downloaded CSE reports (Annual Report 2025 and the Q1, H1 and 9M 2026 interims), keeping the earlier change log and reports read. Cost of equity now from the house CAPM formula with a provisional beta of 0.70 (15.4% base, from 18% hand-set): the main reason fair value rose. Found that nine-month pre-tax profit was flat (−1%) and Q3 pre-tax fell 7%; after-tax growth (+15%) came from finalised prior-year tax assessments (amount not disclosed). Long-run ROE cut a point; 2027 EPS assumes a normal tax rate; dividend model now raises payout to 1 − g/ROE after five years. Beta sources (Damodaran, local betas) only from web-search extracts: the pages were blocked. Business tests 4 of 4; category watch list → buy now (price Rs 154 below the Rs 158 buy price).

Requested from Telegram (/redo SAMP.N0000). No new report; record figures re-checked and the current brief re-applied. All four methods (price to book, P/E, dividends, residual income) now worked by scripts/valuation.py and saved as modelInputs, so the What if? panel works. That changed two methods: the dividend model now keeps the 37% payout throughout (Rs 194 → Rs 133 weighted) and residual income starts every case at 16.5% ROE. Bond rate unchanged at 12.24%, cost of equity still 15.4% (beta 0.70 provisional). Price Rs 154 → Rs 148.25 (CSE close 20 Nov). Business tests 4 of 4; category buy now → watch list (price above the new Rs 144 buy price). Management and shareholders sections not added: no reports in a plain redo.

Requested from Telegram (/redo SAMP.N0000 full). Rebuilt from the four downloaded CSE reports (Annual Report 2025 and the Q1, H1 and 9M 2026 interims), keeping the change log and earlier reports read. Key record figures (9M profit, EPS, NAV, ROE, CET1) spot-checked against the reports: no corrections. Added the management section (Chairman's and CEO's messages, EvolveX plan; promises vs delivery: loan growth and the Rs 20bn Tier 2/green bonds done, capital on track, cost-to-income moving the wrong way) and the shareholders section (top 20 at 30 Sep vs 30 Jun 2026). Price unchanged (Rs 148.25, 20 Nov), calculator gives the same cost of equity and growth check, so the valuation is unchanged. Business tests 4/4; category 2 (watch list), unchanged.

Formula correction (asked by the owner in chat), no new report. scripts/valuation.py's dividend model kept the high-growth payout forever after year 5; it now follows Damodaran's two-stage model (stable payout = 1 − g ÷ ROE). Added eps (from the P/E method) and roe (the long-run ROE the other methods use) to modelInputs.ddm. Only the dividend model changed. The written text still quotes the earlier figures (valuation.textFigures); the page says so until the next update or redo.
